title: The Kiss That Almost Cost You Christ
paragraphs:
The Kiss That Almost Cost You Christ
When Love Feels Right… But Quietly Leads You Away From Jesus
It never starts with rebellion.

It starts with a conversation…
a smile…
a feeling you didn’t pray for but didn’t resist either.

You told yourself, “It’s harmless.”
You said, “God understands.”
You whispered, “This might actually be from Him.”
But deep down… there was a silence in your spirit that didn’t feel like peace.
Because not everything that feels like love… is leading you to Life.
Scripture doesn’t hide from this tension. It confronts it with unsettling clarity. In 2 Corinthians 6:14, Paul writes:
In the original Greek, the phrase ἑτεροζυγοῦντες (heterozygountes) carries the imagery of two animals bound together under one yoke… pulling in different directions… uneven… strained… exhausting.

One is trying to follow Christ.
The other… is not.
And slowly… without realizing it… the stronger pull wins.

Not because you stopped loving Jesus…
but because you got tired of resisting someone you started loving more.
This is where the danger hides.

Because relationships don’t always pull you away from Christ loudly…
sometimes they do it gently…
daily…
subtly…
until one day you wake up and realize you don’t pray like you used to…
you don’t hunger for Scripture like you once did…
and conviction… has gone quiet.
Jesus warned about this kind of divided devotion. In Matthew 6:24, He says:
“No one can serve two masters…”
The Greek word for serve here is δουλεύειν (douleuein) — to be enslaved, bound in loyalty.
Because love… always demands allegiance.

And if someone begins to occupy the space in your heart that belongs to Christ…
you won’t notice the shift immediately.
But heaven does.

This is not about legalism.
This is about lordship.

Because Christ never asked to be part of your life…
He asked to be your life.
And anything… anyone… that competes with that… will eventually pull you.
Even if they never meant to.

Even if they’re kind…
even if they care…
even if they say they support your faith…
If they don’t walk with Christ, they cannot lead you toward Him.
Amos 3:3 asks a haunting question:
“Can two walk together, unless they are agreed?”
In Hebrew, the word יָעַד (ya'ad) implies intentional agreement… a meeting of direction… purpose… destiny.
It’s not just about liking each other.
It’s about walking the same road… toward the same Savior.
Because eventually… someone has to adjust their path.
And too often… it’s the one who once burned for Jesus.
This is how it happens.

You start compromising small things.
You skip prayer to spend time with them.
You silence conviction to keep peace.
You justify distance from God because you don’t want to lose them.
And suddenly…
you’re protecting the relationship more than your relationship with Christ.
But Jesus said something that cuts deeper than comfort ever will:
In Luke 14:26, He declares:
“If anyone comes to Me and does not hate father and mother, wife and children… yes, even their own life—such a person cannot be My disciple.”

The word “hate” here, from the Greek μισεῖ (misei), doesn’t mean emotional hatred…
it means to love less… to prioritize below.
Jesus is not asking for cruelty.
He is demanding supremacy.
Because anything you refuse to surrender… has already taken His place.
And this is where grace enters the scandal.
Because maybe… this isn’t theoretical for you.
Maybe you already feel it.

The distance.
The dullness.
The quiet conviction you’ve been trying to ignore.

Maybe you’re still in it…
holding on…
hoping it changes…
praying they’ll come to Christ eventually…

But if your faith is weakening while you wait…
that’s not love building you.
That’s love costing you.
And Jesus never died for you to slowly drift away while calling it affection.
He died to bring you near.
Ephesians 2:13 says:
“But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.”
The Greek phrase ἐγενήθητε ἐγγὺς (egenēthēte engys) — “brought near” — speaks of intimate closeness… restored access… a relationship sealed by sacrifice.

Why would you trade that…
for a relationship that slowly pulls you back into distance?
This is the moment of honesty.

Not performance.
Not pretending.
Honesty.
Because some of you already know what God has been whispering.
And you’ve been afraid to obey… because obedience might cost you someone you don’t want to lose.
But hear this carefully:

If a relationship pulls you away from Christ…
it is not from Christ.
And anything not from Him… cannot lead you to Him.
This is not about shame.
This is about rescue.
Because grace is not just forgiveness…
it is the power to walk away from what is pulling you away from Him.
So be honest.
You’re not alone in this.
There are others right now… reading this… feeling the same pull… the same tension… the same quiet battle.
Because staying close to truth… is how you stay close to Him.
If you’re ready to go deeper… to be sharpened, corrected, healed, and discipled in truth…
Not out of pressure… but out of purpose.
Because if this message helped you realign your heart toward Christ… imagine what consistent, daily biblical truth can do for your life.
Because following Jesus was never meant to be casual.
It was always meant to cost something.
Just make sure… it’s not costing you Him.
Because the most dangerous relationship isn’t the one that hurts you…
it’s the one that slowly makes you forget how much you need Jesus.
